prompt: A node with no children is called a…
explanation: A leaf has no children. The root is the one node with no parent.

options: Any single edge in the tree
A node together with all of its descendants
The path from the root to a leaf
explanation: A subtree is a node plus everything below it. Each child of a node is the root of a subtree.

prompt: In a BST, which keys are allowed in the LEFT subtree of a node with key 40?
options: Any key smaller than its own parent
explanation: The rule applies to the whole subtree: every key on the left of 40, at any depth, must be smaller than 40.

prompt: A tree where every left child is smaller than its parent and every right child is larger is always a BST. True or false?
explanation: False. Checking only parent and child is not enough. A grandchild can be on the correct side of its parent but the wrong side of an ancestor higher up.

prompt: Why does inserting keys in sorted order (1, 2, 3, 4, 5…) give a lopsided tree?
options: Each new key is larger than every key so far, so it always goes right of the last node
The BST rule stops working for sorted keys
Sorted keys are always placed in the left subtree
Insertion rebalances the tree after every key
explanation: Each new key is bigger than all earlier keys, so it is placed as the right child of the previous key. The tree becomes a chain, like a linked list.

prompt: A balanced BST with 1000 keys has about 10 levels. Roughly how many comparisons does a successful search need at most?
explanation: The worst case equals the number of levels. Each comparison discards a whole subtree, roughly halving what is left.

prompt: The same 1000 keys inserted in sorted order give a chain. How many comparisons does the worst-case search need?
explanation: A chain of 1000 nodes has 1000 levels. Searching for the last key visits every node, just like a linear search through a list.
